source_documents.title: Molecularly Engineered Dual-Emission Pathways with Monomer-Excimer Interplay for Single-Component Blue and White Organic Light-Emitting Diodes

reference_evidence_units.quote: establishing a well-defined intramolecular CT monomer state that shows blue fluorescence
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: HOMO on phenoxazine, LUMO on the DBP acceptor; the monomer emits from an intramolecular CT state.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Assignment supported by DFT and solvatochromism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The steady-state PL spectra of toluene and THF solutions of DBP-PXZ reveal a strong sensitivity of the emission to polarity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ

reference_evidence_units.quote: The dual-band PL spectrum of the film can be assigned to high-energy blue emission from the intramolecular CT S1 state and low-energy greenish-yellow emission from the excimer CT state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dual emission: monomer CT band and excimer CT band.

reference_evidence_units.quote: As the concentration of DBP-PXZ increased, the enhanced proximity among chromophores facilitated stronger intermolecular π-interactions, thereby promoting excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.statement: The low-energy band grows with dopant concentration.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, the dimer exhibits a significantly stabilized S1 state at 2.93 eV
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ dimer model
reference_evidence_units.statement: A modeled dimer has a lower S1 than the monomer (3.10 eV), supporting an intermolecular CT excimer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PLQYs of the solutions of DBP-PXZ are higher than that of the neat film, indicating the absence of aggregation-induced emission enhancement (Table ).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DBP-PXZ
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Says nothing direct about motion restriction.
